title: Prisms & cylinders
examples: How do I find the volume of a cylinder?
What is the formula for the surface area of a prism?
If I know the base area, how do I find the volume?

explain.say: Today we look at prisms and cylinders. These shapes have a consistent cross section. We will learn how to find their volume. Remember volume is the space inside the 3D object.
The formula for volume is really simple to remember. It is the area of the base multiplied by the length. Think of it like stacking layers up.
For a rectangular prism, the base area is length times width. So volume is length times width times height. This is just a special case.
Now let us look at surface area. This is the total area covering the outside. You must find the area of every single face and add them up.

draw.text: Surface Area = Sum of all faces

explain.say: For a cylinder, the surface area has three parts. You need the area of the two circular ends and the curved side. The curved side is like a rectangle.

faq.q: What is the base area for a triangular prism?
faq.a: The base area is the area of the triangle that forms the end. You find this using one half times the base times the height of that triangle.
asks: How do I find the area of the end shape?
What is the area of the base for a triangle?

faq.q: Do I use the radius or the diameter for a cylinder?
faq.a: You must always use the radius, which is half of the diameter. The formula uses the radius, not the diameter.
asks: Should I use r or d?
What measurement goes into the cylinder formula?

faq.q: When calculating surface area, do I include the top and bottom?
faq.a: Yes, you must include the area of both the top and the bottom. These are the two circular ends of the cylinder.
asks: Do I count the circles twice?

faq.q: If the length is given, is that the height for the volume formula?
faq.a: Yes, the length provided is usually the height that you multiply the base area by. It represents how far the shape extends.
asks: Which number do I use for the third dimension?

faq.q: Is the formula for a prism always the same?
faq.a: No, the formula depends on the shape of the base. You must find the area of that specific base shape first.
asks: Is there one single formula for all prisms?

facts: The volume of any prism is found by multiplying the area of its base by its length.
The surface area is the total area of all the faces that make up the outside of the object.
A cylinder is a special type of prism whose base is a circle.
The area of a circle is calculated using the formula pi times the radius squared.

quiz.say: A rectangular block has a base area of 12 square meters and a length of 5 meters. What is its volume?
quiz.why: You multiply the given base area by the length to find the volume.

wrong.1: You added the base area and the length instead of multiplying them.
wrong.2: You forgot to include the unit for volume, which must be cubic units.
wrong.3: You only wrote out the calculation without the final unit.

quiz.say: What is the surface area of a cylinder with a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters?
quiz.why: You must calculate the area of the two circular ends and add it to the area of the curved side.

wrong.0: You only calculated the area of the curved side and forgot the two circular ends.
wrong.1: You multiplied the radius by itself twice when finding the ends.
wrong.2: You incorrectly used the diameter instead of the radius in the formula.

quiz.say: If a prism has a base area of 20 square inches and a height of 4 inches, what is its volume?
quiz.why: The volume is found by multiplying the base area by the height.

wrong.1: You added the base area and the height together.
wrong.2: You forgot to use the cubic unit measurement for volume.
wrong.3: You multiplied the base area by two instead of the height.
